style_context: Video game consoles, PC hardware, and competitive gaming technology across different eras

images.description: Five iconic video game consoles photographed side by side in chronological order from left to right: a wood-paneled Atari 2600 with joystick controller, a gray Nintendo Entertainment System with rectangular controller, an original gray PlayStation console with controller, a black Xbox 360 console with controller, and a Nintendo Switch in its dock with Joy-Con controllers attached. Clean neutral studio background, even lighting, each console clearly distinguishable in size and design.
images.value: Visual side-by-side comparison of console design and size across five hardware generations — the physical evolution is something a reader can only really absorb by seeing the consoles together, not from a list of names and years

images.description: Clean exploded diagram of a desktop gaming PC tower with the case open, showing labeled components: CPU on the motherboard, motherboard itself, RAM sticks in their slots, graphics card (GPU), power supply unit (PSU), storage drive, and case cooling fans. Each component has a short single-word label with a thin leader line pointing to it. Simple, uncluttered technical illustration style with a light background.
images.value: Labeled spatial layout showing where each component physically sits inside the case and how they connect — the physical arrangement and relative size of parts is something text alone cannot convey
